subject: Silverbay: Reliability debrief and commitments
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@silverbay.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@silverbay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Silverbay: Reliability debrief and commitments

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thank you again for flagging the inference reliability problems yesterday. I want to acknowledge the impact: between 08:12–08:57 PT on 2027-10-17 we observed elevated token latencies and an increased 5xx rate that affected approximately 12% of Silverbay production requests (peak error window ~45 minutes). That behavior is below our SLA and unacceptable — apologies for the disruption.

Immediate actions we took:
- Scaled a safe fallback model pool and routed Silverbay traffic there to stabilize latency (completed at 08:22 PT).
- Rolled back a recent kernel-selection rollout that we suspect contributed to the issue (completed at 08:41 PT).
- Enabled aggressive prefix caching for Silverbay's primary routes for the remainder of the day to reduce token pressure.

We are preparing a full RCA and an action tracker with owners and dates; our target for delivery is Wednesday (2027-10-20) EOD PT. I will attach the formal RCA, timeline CSV, and an action-tracker in that follow-up.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review RCA (we will send 10/20).
2) Technical deep-dive with our infra leads (Hannah, Aditya, Jonas) — propose 60 min on Fri 10/22 or Mon 10/25.
3) Agree on remediation verification and request any evidence you need for your internal audit.

If you want a high-level one-pager sooner, I can produce that today — otherwise we will send the full packet on Wednesday.

Again, sorry for the interruption. We take reliability very seriously and will describe corrective work + guardrails in the RCA.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Silverbay: RCA, timeline, and remediation commitments (attached)

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Attached is our full RCA package: silverbay_rca_summary_v1.pdf, silverbay_timeline.csv, and the postmortem-action-tracker.xlsx. Summary and commitments below (TL;DR up front):

Root cause (summary):
- During a staged rollout of an updated kernel-selection policy (deployed 2027-10-16 22:05 PT), a small percentage of requests were routed through a path that bypassed our KV cache optimization. That path was also subject to a new autoscaler heuristic that temporarily underprovisioned CUDA contexts for long-tail sequences. The combination produced increased token-level latency and transient 5xxs when models attempted to access uncached KV entries.

Why it affected Silverbay more:
- Your traffic distribution skewed toward longer sequences during a customer batch (08:10–08:30 PT), which amplified the underprovisioning window and made cache misses more likely.

Timeline (high level):
- 2027-10-16 22:05 PT: Kernel-selection policy rollout begins (canary subset).
- 2027-10-17 07:58 PT: Monitoring alerts for elevated p95/p99 latency for route silverbay-main.
- 2027-10-17 08:12 PT: Error rate begins rising; consumer retries observed.
- 2027-10-17 08:22 PT: Fallback routing to stable pool enabled for silverbay-main; latency improves.
- 2027-10-17 08:41 PT: Kernel-selection rollback completed for all canary hosts.
- 2027-10-17 09:05 PT: All systems returned to baseline.

Action items and owners (short):
1) Add canary guardrails to kernel-selection pipeline to block routes with >10% long-sequence traffic during rollout windows — Owner: Hannah Schmitt — Due: 2027-11-03.
2) Modify autoscaler heuristic to account for sequence-length distribution and reserve CUDA contexts for long-tail requests — Owner: Aditya Rao — Due: 2027-11-10.
3) Add end-to-end synthetic traffic test that mirrors Silverbay long-sequence patterns to our pre-rollout harness — Owner: Jonas Weber — Due: 2027-10-29.
4) Provide Silverbay a one-off verification run and verified metrics package for 10/25 — Owner: Mina Haddad — Due: 2027-10-25.
5) Update runbook to include explicit cache-validation checks and alert thresholds — Owner: Hannah Schmitt — Due: 2027-11-03.

SLA credits and next steps:
- We will calculate credit eligibility based on the documented SLA and deliver a credit estimate by 2027-10-22. Priya, we'll include the calculations and the claim form in that packet.

Attached files include metric exports, sampled logs (redacted), timeline CSV, and the action tracker with task rows and Jira links. For convenience: Jira RW-2109 contains the engineering remediation epics. Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/silverbay/RCAs/2027-10-20

Proposed follow-up:
- Technical deep-dive (60m) with infra owners: Fri 2027-10-22 10:00 PT or Mon 2027-10-25 11:00 PT — please confirm availability.

If you want us to prioritize any of the action items (e.g., earlier autoscaler changes), we can escalate.

Thanks again and sorry for the disruption. We will also deliver a short postmortem one-pager suitable for your internal stakeholders.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Mina / team —

Thanks for the thorough analysis and for the clear owners/deadlines. We reviewed the summary and attachments; a few quick notes:
- We appreciate the concrete action dates. Please prioritize the autoscaler heuristic change (Aditya) — that one has the highest risk-to-production for our workload.
- We confirm the technical deep-dive on Fri 2027-10-22 10:00 PT works for our engineers.
- Regarding credits: we will await the calculation packet on 10/22 and will route it through procurement once received.

Can you also include the sampled trace IDs referenced in the logs so our team can correlate with our telemetry? If redaction is necessary, include mapping instructions.

Thanks — look forward to the dd.

Best,
